title: Documentation
subtitle: Step-by-step guide, chunk gate, weighted validation scoring, and sensitivity levels.
aboutP1: GenA (Generation & Sensitivity Assessment) is a dynamic Russian-language framework designed to address the gap between classical question generation (QG) and practical requirements for legally accurate, socially safe questions. It gives users a controllable, transparent tool while minimizing conflict risks associated with sensitive topics (cultural, historical, and linguistic).
aboutContributions: The framework provides three key contributions:
aboutC1: from Russian texts (encyclopedias, regulatory legal acts, and legal documents).
aboutC2: that reflect conflict potential within sociocultural contexts.
aboutC3: Dual-validation combined with human review lets users evaluate quality, accept or reject questions, and confirm or modify sensitivity levels.
sensIntro: Each question receives a sensitivity annotation from 1 to 3, based on the perceived probability of conflict within a given sociocultural context:
sens1Desc: Neutral topics that do not foster discussion or differences of opinion.
sens2Desc: Controversial or ambiguous topics. Different viewpoints exist but are not radically opposed; discussions may spark debate without serious conflict.
sens3Desc: Highly sensitive cultural, historical, or political topics. Responses may require expressing personal opinions on contentious issues.
sensOutro: Users evaluate both generation quality and sensitivity-level appropriateness, forming a feedback loop for continuous improvement.
typeOneDesc: one correct answer from multiple options.
typeMultiDesc: several correct answers from the options provided.
howto1Body: Go to Create questions and upload a file. Supported formats: .docx, .txt, .pdf. Pick the document name and settings right away — chunking runs later in the background generation.
howto2Title: Select question types and configure generation
howto2Body: Choose one or more question types (one, multi, open).
howto2Note: By default all three types are selected. Clearing the selection resets it to all three — you cannot run generation with an empty list.
howto2Models: Model selection — pick the LLM for generation (questions, sensitivity, difficulty) and for validation (chunk gate + scoring).
howto2Queue: Background generation — after you click Generate, chunking, gate, and generation all run in the worker. You can close the tab and track progress on the Progress page.
howto3Body: Click «Generate questions». The app creates a generation, uploads the document, and enqueues a chunking task. The worker then:
howto3Chunk: Chunk — split the document into passages.
howto3Gate: Gate — check each passage for suitability; failing passages are discarded.
howto3Gen: Generate — create questions for every passage that passed the gate (one task per type).
howto3Note: If the gate rejects every passage, the dataset finishes with status no_valid_chunks — nothing to generate.
howto4Body: Use Generation Progress to see every generation with its status, tasks, fragments, questions and progress; the Administration section shows model health and lets you retry failed tasks.
howto5Body: In My questions each item shows its task, answer options with the correct ones marked, sensitivity and difficulty with the model's rationale, the quality validation result with an explanation of failed criteria, and the source chunk. Edits are saved per question into the selected version; questions can be excluded from export, and the set can be downloaded as Excel, GIFT, or printed.
howto6Body: Use Download XLSX in My questions to export generation results (and optional full-pipeline data) as a spreadsheet.
howto7Body: The Analytics page shows aggregated analytics: question-type, sensitivity, and difficulty distributions, validation pass rates, and processing-status breakdown.
gateIntro: Before generation, every chunk is assessed by a gate using the validation model. Three binary criteria are checked:
gateC1: c1 — Informative: does the chunk contain enough substance for a question?
gateC2: c2 — Reference clarity: is the chunk understandable without external sources?
gateC3: c3 — Multi suitability (only for multi): can the chunk support plausible wrong answers?
gateOutro: If c1 or c2 fails, the chunk is discarded entirely. If c3 fails, only multi tasks are skipped — one and open can still proceed.
gateNote: The gate runs as background queue tasks after chunking. Rejected passages never get generation tasks. If every passage is rejected, the run ends with no_valid_chunks.
chunksIntro: Chunks are stored separately from datasets in a dedicated chunks collection, linked by dataset_id. Each record holds the text, fragment metadata, gate results, and the question types it is valid for. This keeps dataset queries lightweight and lets chunks be re-processed independently.
chunksTable: The Existing Datasets table on Create questions shows the chunk count (valid / total) per dataset.
validationIntro: Every generated question goes through automated quality validation that checks:
validation1: Factual correctness against the source text
validationScoring: Scoring. Sub-criteria are combined using weights; several are critical multipliers: if any scores zero, the overall total becomes zero. The reported score can be a decimal (e.g. 15.5 / 20.5).
validationOutro: Validation produces a numeric score and a pass/fail verdict against a configurable threshold. Experts can then review, override, and refine the results in the editor.
